theme: Christ above all; the cosmic Christ; the mystery
readingInstruction: Read Colossians 1:1-2:5. This is the great passage on the supremacy of Christ. Read verses 15-20 slowly and several times. Then notice how Paul describes his own ministry of suffering and labor.
settingTheScene: Paul wrote Colossians from prison to a church he had not founded, in a town in the Lycus Valley near Laodicea and Hierapolis. Epaphras had planted the church and brought news of a developing heresy. The false teaching mixed Jewish regulations, mystical visions, angel worship, and ascetic practices with a diminished view of Christ. Paul’s answer is not a list of rules but a magnificent portrait of Christ as supreme over everything.
observation: “He has delivered us from the domain of darkness and transferred us to the kingdom of his beloved Son” (1:13).
“He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation” (1:15).
“For by him all things were created, in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible” (1:16).
“And he is before all things, and in him all things hold together” (1:17).
“And he is the head of the body, the church. He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, that in everything he might be preeminent” (1:18).
“Making peace by the blood of his cross” (1:20).
“Christ in you, the hope of glory” (1:27).
“In whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge” (2:3).
interpretation:
Paul greets the church, thanks God for their faith, love, and hope, and prays that they would be filled with the knowledge of God’s will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding, to walk in a manner worthy of the Lord, fully pleasing to him, bearing fruit, increasing in the knowledge of God, strengthened with all power, joyfully giving thanks to the Father. And he states what God has done: “He has delivered us from the domain of darkness and transferred us to the kingdom of his beloved Son, in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins.”

Then the hymn to Christ in verses 15 to 20. In the first stanza, Christ is supreme over creation. “He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation. For by him all things were created, in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities, all things were created through him and for him. And he is before all things, and in him all things hold together.” “Image” means that he perfectly shows God. “Firstborn” is a title of rank and inheritance, not of being created: he is the heir and sovereign over creation, as the creator of it. Everything was made by him, through him, and for him. He holds the universe together. No angel, spirit, or power rivals him.

In the second stanza, Christ is supreme over the new creation. “He is the head of the body, the church. He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, that in everything he might be preeminent. For in him all the fullness of God was pleased to dwell, and through him to reconcile to himself all things, whether on earth or in heaven, making peace by the blood of his cross.” The creator is the redeemer. The same Christ who made all things is reconciling all things. The cross is the means of cosmic peace. Notice that “all the fullness of God” dwells in him.

Then Paul applies it to the Colossians: once alienated and hostile in mind, doing evil deeds, they have been reconciled in his body of flesh by his death, “in order to present you holy and blameless and above reproach before him, if indeed you continue in the faith.” Perseverance is the evidence of reality.

Paul describes his own ministry. He rejoices in his sufferings for their sake, “and in my flesh I am filling up what is lacking in Christ’s afflictions for the sake of his body, that is, the church.” This does not mean Christ’s atonement is incomplete; rather, Paul’s sufferings as an apostle extend Christ’s afflictions into the world as the gospel is spread. The mystery now revealed is “Christ in you, the hope of glory.” He proclaims Christ, warning everyone and teaching everyone in all wisdom, that he may present everyone mature in Christ. Chapter 2 begins with his struggle for them, that their hearts may be encouraged, knit together in love, to reach all the riches of full assurance of understanding and of knowing the mystery of God, “in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.”
connection: Genesis 1 and Proverbs 8:22-31 stand behind the creation language. John 1:1-3 and Hebrews 1:1-4 are parallel statements. Isaiah 45:18 and Psalm 33:6 speak of God as creator. Revelation 1:5 calls Jesus the firstborn of the dead. Romans 8:19-23 speaks of creation’s renewal. Ephesians 1:10 and 2:11-22 speak of uniting all things. 2 Corinthians 5:18-21 speaks of reconciliation. Philippians 2:5-11 is a related hymn. Galatians 2:20 speaks of Christ living in us.
application:
Read Colossians 1:15-20 aloud once a day this week. Let it enlarge your view of Christ.

Where do you feel small in the face of problems? Remember that he holds all things together.

Ask what it means for you that Christ is “preeminent in everything.” What area of your life does he not yet lead?
prayerPrompts: Worship Jesus as the image of the invisible God.
Thank him that in him all things hold together.
Tell him what you want to give him preeminence over.
